sentences.text: The genus name Cryptarcus translates as “hidden arch”.
The holotype preserves most of an articulated skull, although the front snout, lower jaws, right half of the frill and portions of the left face were absent and later rebuilt in plaster.
Its frill shows a median embayment whose angle varies from 89° to 128°, a measurement that helps separate it from Chasmosaurus belli.
The skull of the holotype measures about 94 cm in length.
The parietosquamosal frill extends to roughly 120 % of the skull’s length.
A short, broad-based nasal horn sits over the rear of the naris.
Postorbital horns survive only as small stumps, which may reflect pathology, though they could have been longer in life.
A pronounced rugose area is present on each palpebral bone just in front of the eyes.
The frontoparietal fontanelle is unusually wide and bears a distinctive bone bridge between the postorbitals, likely an age-related feature.
The type species, Cryptarcus russelli, was first described under the name Chasmosaurus russelli by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1940.
Phylogenetic studies place Cryptarcus in an unresolved polytomy, sometimes nearer to Pentaceratops and other times nearer to Chasmosaurus, depending on the analysis.
When only the holotype is considered, three consensus topologies emerge, positioning it variously closer to Chasmosaurus, closer to Pentaceratops, or remaining unresolved.
Cryptarcus is known from the Dinosaur Park Formation and dates to the middle Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

Researchers have argued over whether specimens previously assigned to Chasmosaurus russelli represent a distinct genus, with Nick Longrich proposing the name Mojoceratops perifania in 2010, a view that most other scientists reject.
Traits once thought to link Cryptarcus with Chasmosaurus, such as a low facial profile and a thin parietal strut, also appear in other chasmosaurines and may be influenced by post-mortem distortion.
The authors reported no phylogenetic support for the previously suggested anagenetic sequence from Cryptarcus russelli through Pentaceratops to Terminocavus.
